trigger: On an offer() timeout, the drain worker is not woken when the delayed send later completes - it waits for the next enqueue or the periodic backstop
summary: Cadence regression versus pre-fix behavior: pre-fix a 300ms send blocked the loop inline and the next tick started as soon as it returned; post-fix a send between kGuardianSendOfferWait (200ms) and the periodic backstop (kDefaultPeriodicBoundMs, 5s in production) hits Retain and waits for the backstop - e.g. a 300ms send waits roughly 16x its own duration, up to roughly 25x for a send finishing just past the 200ms threshold, shrinking toward 1x near the backstop. A completion-waker fix was built and wired, then REVERTED after it broke a pre-existing refill-rearm timing test; not fixed in this PR.

trigger: offer() releases state_->mu after deciding need_launch=true but before calling launch(); launch() did not re-check state_->stopping, so a concurrent GuardianOutboxDrainWorker::stop() landing in that gap did not prevent a new detached send from being admitted
summary: found independently by both adversarial reviewers (codex C1, claude F3, both confirmed by direct code read); not a UAF/unjoined-thread/data-race (orphan-exit sum stays correct throughout), and requires a second independent stall to matter, but is a genuine violation of stop()'s documented no-new-launch promise on a compile-time-dormant path. Fixed operator-directed: launch() now re-checks state_->stopping under state_->mu as the first statement in its locked bookkeeping block, synchronized against stop() via the same mutex. A test-only race hook (set_pre_launch_race_hook_for_test, matching spark_engine.hpp's established *_hook_for_test_ pattern) was added to make the fix mutation-verifiable RED-then-GREEN without relying on real thread-scheduling luck. Impact reclassified I5->I8 at Gate 8 re-review (consistency-auditor): the pre-fix consequence was bounded and fully accounted for by the orphan-exit contract, requiring a second independent stall to matter - structurally closer to p1-spawn-detached-bad-alloc-miscounted (I8/LOW) than an unavailability finding in its own right. severity_mapped now matches both external reviewers' native LOW.

trigger: GuardianOutboxDrainWorker::stop() sets sig_->stopping (the flag drain_bounded()'s should_stop() reads before every send), then calls lifecycle_send_exec_.stop() and compliance_send_exec_.stop() as two SEPARATE, sequential, non-atomic steps afterward - not under one lock with the flag write
summary: A structurally identical admission race to adv-codex-c1-toctou, one call frame further out: the drain worker's own thread can observe should_stop()==false (queried before sig_->stopping lands) and enter wrapped_send() for a lane whose own executor .stop() has not yet been called, admitting a send after the caller had already begun shutdown. Bounded the same way as C1/F3 (orphan-exit contract still counts it correctly, AliveTicket/active_send_workers() unaffected, not a UAF/data race/wedge) and on the same compile-time-dormant path (prefer_spark_=false). No test-only hook was built to force this interleave deterministically (epistemic_status likely, not verified) - would need its own seam at the GuardianOutboxDrainWorker::stop() level, structurally the same approach as C1/F3's fix.

Fixed: offer()'s reclaim path on a mismatched orphan now increments orphan_exceptions_discarded and logs on first occurrence when the reclaimed result was a thrown exception, rather than discarding it with no signal. Test: "#3953 item 1: a reclaimed orphan's thrown exception is counted, not just silently discarded" (test_guardian_outbox_send_executor.cpp), mutation-verified RED before the fix.

Fixed: a send exceeding a stall threshold (production default 5s) is now counted (send_stall_count()) and logged once, with a matching recovery log on eventual completion/reclaim - covering the same-entry timeout case, a send crossing the threshold during one bounded wait, and a mismatched orphan stalled indefinitely. Measured against completion time, not observation time. Surfaced on the heartbeat as yuzu.guardian_send_stalls (a32c989af). Three tests in test_guardian_outbox_send_executor.cpp, mutation-verified RED before the fix.

Fixed with an internal wait clamp, not a completion-waker (the previously-reverted approach that broke R4): GuardianOutboxDrainWorker::loop() polls has_in_flight_send() on both lane executors after every drain pass and clamps its own wait to kGuardianSendRecheckInterval (200ms) while anything is in flight - a wait-only change, no wake source, so R4 ("a refill re-arm does not wait out the periodic bound") is untouched by construction (its sink is fully synchronous). Detection latency after completion now bounded by roughly kGuardianSendOfferWait + kGuardianSendRecheckInterval instead of the periodic backstop (~16-25x improvement). Two tests (executor-level accessor coverage + drain-worker-level cadence, test_guardian_outbox_send_executor.cpp / test_guardian_outbox_drain_worker.cpp), mutation-verified RED before the fix.

Two tests in test_guardian_outbox.cpp, mutation-verified RED before the fix (via a temporary revert of the domain check).

This row's own "drain()'s comment already discloses this exact residual" claim was itself an overclaim, corrected rather than repeated: the disclosure named only sequential/next-pass cases (a reconnect flap between phases, a concurrent arm during the compliance phase), never the SAME-PASS two-executor mechanism this finding is actually about, and sat on drain() rather than the production drain_bounded() path. guardian_spark_runtime.cpp's drain()/drain_bounded() and guardian_outbox_drain_worker.hpp's wrapped_send() doc comments corrected to name the real mechanism and point at #3972 ("Guardian outbox: cross-lane wire reordering - merge-drain by global sequence"), filed with full dedupe (checked #3848/#2993/#3953/#3966/#2237, none cover it). deferred-to-issue, not rejected: rejected means an INVALID (false/inapplicable/disproven) finding per SKILL.md, and this finding is real.

Fixed with the same technique as #3966 (adv-codex-c1-toctou), one call frame further out: GuardianOutboxDrainWorker::stop() now stops both lane executors FIRST, unconditionally, before publishing sig_->stopping - closing the window where the drain loop could observe should_stop()==false and admit a send on a lane whose own executor had not yet been told to stop. Deterministic falsifier (set_stop_race_hook_for_test firing in the old gap) mutation-verified RED before the fix: the hook observed a send wrongly admitted (Sent, one invocation) instead of refused (Retain, zero invocations). CH-1 (stop()-shutdown-latency, <400ms) and R4 re-verified green - this item touches only stop(), not loop()'s wait computation.
